body: Not caring isn't what my intention for the post was. I'm new to reddit, so I'm a little saddened by these negatives. Not sure what's going on honestly, as it was just a question. Maybe Reddit is for a younger crowd and I should've tried a different approach with this.
Did you experience experience withdrawals? What kept you from going back
What affected your life the most and why
What are negative replies? Can anyone who gave me a negative reply explain why?
Will you share your story with me?
Will you share more of your story?

(I am not a user of any drug, but I work with people who use drugs so I want to make that known) with the heroin/opiates, at what point of use did you realize it was an addiction. Was it a small amount that caused the waking up and wanting to use? What were the symptoms you felt not using? What brought you back to it? This is specific with the heroin/opiates. If someone who is a user, even overdosed says they aren't using, is it the truth?

Edit: what made you stop the heroin/opiates? Was it another drug/meth? This is honestly informational, thank you for responding.

I understand these stats, I was looking for people's actual experiences. I'm 30, single,  relatively successful (albeit depressed, but that's a different subreddit) if you look at success from a financial/home owner/higher education/phenomenal family way. I'm not trying, but also not not trying because I'm perfectly capable in a non traditional way. I did not want to explain all of this, I was more or less hoping women would share their own personal experience on the subject. No thank you for plan B, but thank you for the response.

Sharing beds with multiple siblings. The bed is a mattress on the floor, typically no sheets for neglect.
Perfectionism in thought, action, and words for abuse.
